criteria.criterion: Initiates interview correctly: introduction, name, role, purpose
Addresses confidentiality and sets time frame
Uses open-ended opening question
PQRST — Provocation and Palliation
PQRST — Quality and Region (radiation)
PQRST — Severity (0-10 scale) and Timing
ROS: dyspnoea, PND, orthopnoea, palpitations, oedema
Past Medical History: HTN, DM, medications, adherence
Family History: premature cardiac disease
Allergy history including reaction type
Lifestyle: smoking pack-years, alcohol
ADL impact explored
Accurate comprehensive closing summary confirmed
Identifies correct system with rationale
Empathetic communication throughout
Prepares correctly: hand hygiene, explains, positions at 45 degrees
Inspects precordium: apex visibility, scars, contour
Selects apex beat palpation when clinically indicated and correctly documents or interprets the resulting findings
Correctly assesses and interprets apex beat location and left ventricular heave, recognizing normal or abnormal findings when clinically relevant
Selects assessment for cardiac thrills when clinically indicated and correctly documents or interprets their presence or absence
Selects cardiac auscultation with the diaphragm and correctly documents or interprets the resulting heart sounds and rhythm findings
Performs appropriate cardiac auscultation with the bell and correctly identifies the presence or absence of additional heart sounds, including S3 when present
Selects carotid auscultation when clinically indicated and correctly documents or interprets the resulting findings, including the presence or absence of bruits
Correctly documents or interprets carotid auscultation findings when the assessment is clinically indicated, without requiring unverified technique details
Inspects upper extremities: colour, oedema, clubbing
Selects upper extremity pulse assessment when clinically appropriate and correctly documents or interprets the resulting pulse findings

Selects lower extremity inspection when clinically indicated and correctly documents or interprets the resulting findings, including skin changes, swelling, or other visible abnormalities when present
Selects lower extremity pulse assessment when clinically indicated and correctly documents or interprets the resulting pulse findings
Selects peripheral oedema assessment when clinically indicated and correctly documents or interprets its absence or severity when present
Assesses capillary refill upper and lower extremities
Maintains privacy, dignity, communicates throughout
Verbalises all findings (positive and negative) as elicited
Follows correct systematic sequence
Correctly interprets JVP findings as normal or elevated and explains their clinical significance when relevant to the patient's presentation
Correctly interprets cardiac auscultation findings and explains their clinical significance when relevant, without assuming abnormal heart sounds are present
Documents patient identity and date
Summarises interview accurately and completely
Documents examination findings with correct terminology
Records all abnormal findings and relevant normal findings
Identifies all major clinical problems in priority order
Documents problem with supporting clinical evidence
States referral decision with urgency level
Includes required referral information
Report is organised and clinically structured
No clinically dangerous omissions
Correctly determines whether referral is required and selects an appropriate urgency level based on the patient's symptoms, examination findings, and clinical risk
Selects an appropriate referral destination or explains why referral is not required, based on the patient's clinical condition and level of urgency
Correctly determines and documents the appropriate urgency level, including emergency, urgent, routine, or no immediate referral, based on the patient's clinical presentation

Identifies appropriate immediate nursing actions based on the patient's clinical condition, including patient safety, monitoring, escalation when indicated, and actions required before referral if applicable
Provides a clinically appropriate justification for the referral or non-referral decision, supported by the patient's symptoms, assessment findings, risk factors, and relevant clinical evidence
